title: ci: stop the client type-check ratchet from filing npm's header as a file
intent: The type-check ratchet's per-file report was wrong on every CI run. CI pipes `npm run type-check` through `tee`, so npm's `> @production-shop/client@1.0.0 type-check` / `> vue-tsc --noEmit` header comes right before the first diagnostic. ERROR_RE's file group (`[^(]*?`) could cross line breaks, so the match began at the header's `>` and ran on to the first `(line,col)`. The first error was then filed under a key made of the header text plus `src/api/profiling.ts`. The total stayed correct, so the gate itself still blocked correctly. But the 'Files above their baseline' report always contained a phantom line. On PR #430 it read `src/api/profiling.ts: 0 -> 1` beside the real regression, although profiling.ts was unchanged. That points developers at the wrong file and can hide the real source of a future regression.
behavior_change: Per-file attribution in the ratchet's FAIL report and in --write-baseline output is now correct when the log contains npm's header (always, in CI). The pass/fail decision is unchanged, because it depends only on the total count, and the total was already correct. The ceiling (total_errors 150) and the committed baseline are not modified. The baseline's by_file already records src/api/profiling.ts: 2 correctly; only the reading of CI logs was wrong. Two CI wiring changes: (1) core_ci.yml runs the new parser tests on every PR. (2) client_lint_build.yml now also triggers on changes to the ratchet script and its baseline. Before this, a PR that edited only the ratchet or raised the ceiling never ran the gate it changed.

diff_articulation.what_changed: ERROR_RE's file group changes from `[^(]*?` to `[^(\r\n]*?`, so a match cannot cross a line break, with a comment recording why. New scripts/ci/test_client_type_check_ratchet.py (11 tests, stdlib-only). Its fixtures are copied from PR #430's real lint-build log (run 37291225924), including the npm header and an indented continuation line. The tests cover: the header is never part of a file key; the same diagnostics with and without the header parse identically; continuation lines are not counted; CRLF logs; Windows backslash paths normalize to POSIX; --write-baseline from a CI-shaped log writes no header keys; unchanged diagnostics PASS with no per-file movement; a real new error is reported against its own file and no other; checking never rewrites the baseline; and the committed baseline has no header, multi-line or backslash keys, with by_file summing to total_errors.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: No existing test covered the ratchet's parser. The defect was only visible as a misleading line in a FAIL report, and the gate only prints that report when it is already failing for a real reason. That is exactly when nobody questions the file list.

commands_run: Defect reproduced from PR #430's CI log: the FAIL report listed `src/api/profiling.ts: 0 -> 1` although that file's two errors are byte-identical under vue-tsc 3.3.11 and 3.3.12
Same tests against origin/main's unmodified parser -> 7 failed, 4 passed (the 4 that pass do not depend on header attribution), so the tests detect the defect
Full real log, 150 errors with npm header (main 2a2f3924 tree): per-file counts vs committed baseline -> 0 differences
Full real log, 152 errors with npm header (PR #430 pre-fix): FAIL report now lists exactly `src/views/cam/headstock/WorkspaceView.vue: 21 -> 23`, no phantom profiling.ts line

files.intent: Bound ERROR_RE's file group to a single line.
files.behavior_change: Correct per-file attribution; the gate decision is unchanged.

files.intent: Regression tests built from the real CI log shape.
Run the parser tests on every PR. Nothing else collects scripts/ci/ wholesale, so an unpinned test would never run.
files.behavior_change: One additional test step in Core CI.

files.intent: Trigger the client lint-build (which runs the ratchet) when the ratchet script or its baseline changes.
files.behavior_change: lint-build now also runs on PRs touching those two files.

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: CI tooling only; no application code or architectural surface touched.
